title: A linear sodium correction removes up to 74 percent of 35.68-day orbital information in 56 GJ 832 observations from 2019
abstract: We test a linear sodium activity correction in public GJ 832 HARPS data. With a linear slow trend and a fixed 2 m/s weight floor, the correction removes 74.0 percent of orbital information for one phase of a 35.68-day circular wave in 56 observations from 2019. The least retained fraction is 0.254 to 0.308 across six weight and trend choices. Sequential removal can reduce a unit injected amplitude to 0.255; a joint fit avoids this synthetic bias but loses information. The sodium correction raises held-out squared error by 2.8 to 20.6 percent in six main block tests. An early fitted sodium slope gives only a 0.066 percent later error reduction, which changes sign with the slow model. The result is an audit of a specified correction, not evidence for a planet or a new rejection of the disputed planet. Shared spectra, index error, correlated noise, and a short later time span limit physical inference. We include original code, aggregate results, a figure, exact source hashes and a separate-scratch retrieval script. External observation rows are excluded from the baseline bundle.

display.caption: The specified activity correction can remove orbital information without giving a stable held-out prediction gain. The figure uses a linear slow trend and a 2 m/s weight floor.

citations.reason: Motivates a distinct correction audit and defines the time groups. We reuse its public shared input paths, not its code or fitted results.
